headline: Spain's Relentless Wastefulness Lets Cabo Verde Off
story: Spain controlled this entirely. Pedri orchestrated the midfield, Cucurella drove the left flank, and the visitors rarely threatened the Laporte-anchored defence. Spain pressed 10.3 high-press phases, forcing 53 turnovers in Cabo Verde's half. The home team fired 27 shots—seven on target—and registered 2.26 expected goals. Yet Cabo Verde, compact and disciplined in their 4-1-4-1, scraped a draw through sheer imperviousness. The shape was always Spain attacking; the puzzle was never breaking through.

Four clear chances went begging: a post at 39', a block at 40', a save at 56', and a miss at 45+4'. Vozinha, the visiting keeper, delivered a 9.0 performance, made the crucial 56th-minute stop, and steadied the ship. Spain's 66% possession and relentless press couldn't overcome their own profligacy. Cabo Verde's ball-recovery time of 24.8 seconds meant they were slow to transition, yet their defensive shape held. Sometimes you need just one moment; Spain's wasteful shooting meant Cabo Verde got to leave with pride and a point.

keyMoment.text: Vozinha's save denied Spain again—the moment their dominance required a goal.

home.verdict: Controlled but profligate—pressing created chaos, but finishing proved elusive.
points: Four big chances missed (39', 40', 56', 45+4')—clinical conversion wins tournaments.
2.26 xG with 27 shots: volume without incision is just noise.
Possess and press, but they still needed ruthlessness in the box.

away.verdict: Disciplined retreat, exceptional goalkeeper work—a smash-and-grab point.
points: Vozinha's 9.0 rating: the 56th-minute save was the difference between draw and defeat.
24.8-second recovery time slowed Spain's transitions; compact shape suffocated creativity.
0.13 xG but zero conceded—defensive solidity overcame complete possession surrender.

statLine: Spain created 2.26 expected goals from 27 shots; Vozinha's 9.0-rated performance and Cabo Verde's immovable shape ensured a scoreless stalemate.
